messages:
maya: quick update from the zephyr-lite quant canary run. int4 route shows an uptick in funcall parse failures vs int8 baseline. starting sample: 600 requests. parse_failures: 18 (3.0%) vs baseline ~0.5%.

alex: ouch. any obvious pattern in the broken outputs?

maya: pattern: concatenation artifacts where kv-prefix merging inserts or leaves punctuation at the join. examples vary: trailing commas, duplicated closing brace, or a partial NDJSON line appended. single-line example: `...\"arguments\":{\"q\":\"x\"},}` -> extra `}`.

sam: does the funcall contract allow NDJSON? we've talked about NDJSON as a mitigation before.

rachel: NDJSON would give us simple line-splitting recovery, but client and logging changes needed. Might be faster to add a lightweight runtime adapter first.

maya: agreed. proposed immediate mitigations: 1) small prompt guard: add \"Respond strictly with valid JSON only, no trailing commas or extra characters.\" 2) runtime adapter: opt-in per-route sanitizer that tries a sequence: ndjson-split -> last-json-extract -> punctuation-trim -> regex-trailing-comma-strip. Each attempted repair gets tagged. 3) int4 canary route with kv-prefix disabled for 1% traffic to measure delta.

alex: what's the regex for trailing comma strip? we need something conservative.

maya: using: `s/,\s*(?=[}\]])//g` in the parser stage (JS flavor lookahead). runs only when parse fails and diagnostics indicate a single trailing comma.

sam: unit tests? we should have a corpus of valid and intentionally weird cases. include nested arrays/objects and strings with commas.

rachel: add a safety net: if sanitizer changes structure (length delta > 500 chars or changes token count significantly) mark as \"sanitizer_rejected\" and don't apply. We should never pretend we repaired when we didn't.

ci-bot: job started: job/zephyr-int4-kv-adapt-3490 (600 samples) -> https://ci.redwood/job/zephyr-int4-kv-adapt-3490

maya: I'll open a PR for the adapter + telemetry keys today. telemetry fields: `parse_outcome` (ok/repaired/failed), `repair_method` (none,ndjson,lastjson,strip_comma,trim_chars), `kvprefix_enabled` (true/false), `model_quant` (int8/int4).

alex: add `repair_latency_ms` and `sanitizer_applied` boolean so we can see perf tradeoffs.

sam: also capture `original_suffix` length bucket: small/medium/large so we can tell whether long suffixes are more repairable.

maya: plan for rollout: opt-in per-route flag + feature-flag gate. couple of safety guards: max repairs per-request = 1, and we double-tag requests that hit repaired+fallback so product can triage.

rachel: what about changing prompts or contracts? Would asking models to output a single top-level JSON object (instead of embedding text) help?

sam: it helps but quantized models still hallucinate punctuation. runtime adapters are the most reliable immediate fix.

maya: timeline: PR today, unit tests and harness added, canary job runs now, initial dashboards within 24h. I'll post numbers (repair rate, p95 latency delta, fallback count).

alex: once results are in, let's evaluate longer-term options: NDJSON contract, explicit boundary sentinel, or moving key-value merging out of the token stream (i.e., attach metadata instead of concatenation).

maya: agreed. creating an issue to track long-term: INF-2219: funcall boundary strategy.

ci-bot: job finished: job/zephyr-int4-kv-adapt-3490 -> success (600 samples) summary: parse_failures: 17 -> repaired: 11 (repair_latency_median=72ms,p95=260ms) fallbacks: 6. Dashboard: https://ci.redwood/dash/zephyr-int4-kv-adapt-3490

sam: thanks for the quick triage. post the PR link when ready and tag the release notes.

maya: PR: https://git.redwood/pr/4382 (adapter + telemetry + harness). comments welcome. I'll coordinate release gating if canary looks good tomorrow.
